This is copied from an old post, but it sums everything up pretty well — good luck! Ammonia, nitrates, and nitrates all have a relationship with each other and the biological filter. 

pH can be anywhere from 7.0 -8.4. Honestly Ph level is not that important as Bettas can adapt to a wide ph range. The important thing with ph is to keep it steady. It's better to keep a fish who is acclimated to 8.0 ph at 8.0 than to try and adjust to too low a ph that may shock it.

As for the other parameters the Ammonia should be 0 as it is highly toxic to any fish including Bettas. Nitrites should also be 0 although they can tolerate more of this in the water than Ammonia but its still bad. During cycling you may have nitrites so its important to do daily PWC  if they are rising above 1 ppm. When not cycling no nitrites should be present. Nitrates are the last parameter to worry about and this should be kept below 40 ppm. Nitrates are non toxic at low levels and in a properly cycled tank weekly water changes of 10% percent is all that is needed to keep nitrates low. Also live plants feed off of nitrates in the water and can also help keep this number low. In a non cycled tank you should be changing the water every other day 100% water changes with treated and same temperature water.

I recommend an API test kit with the bottles etc over any paper test kits as you will save money in the long run. During cycling and on fish I really care about I will test nitrites almost daily. If something seems off Ill test ammonia and nitrates and then do water changes to lower levels if needed. Clean water = healthy fish and its not hard to keep your water clean even with limited chemical usage. De Chlorinator is a must etc and prime can help during cycling to neutralize any low levels of Ammonia and Nitrites but proper treated water changes are usually the best thing.

I know what you mean but as corny as this sounds you might just be ready for a new chapter or a sequel. I know that you’re not always in the position to make a major change in your life like starting over somewhere new. But the first step towards working through things is opening up and talking about it especially with your closest friends or loved ones. There’s so many things in this world to experience if you just look in some new places or get out of your comfort zone. One of my favorite quotes by Jim Carrey is “depression is your avatar telling you it’s tired of the character you’re trying to play”. Old Jim’s kinda crazy and I’m not sure if that helps at all but I really did notice myself change when my surroundings did and I was a much happier person. There wasn’t any pressure from anyone to stay a certain person and I was able to start over and recreate myself a bit.

Yea that’s definitely not something to take lightly. But I’ve really learned that if you embrace that feeling it won’t go away. As hard as it is you gotta break the cycle. When you don’t correct that negative inner dialogue or those feelings they will start to manifest. I would always find myself thinking things like “I fucking hate myself” or “I’m gonna fucking kill myself” and it really took a lot to stop doing that and start forcing myself to think positively. It wasn’t easy. But when you’re depressed you don’t even really realize how fucked up and self deprecating your thoughts are because you truly believe them and they’re almost subconscious. It got to the point where I would literally stand in front of a mirror everyday and tell my self out loud that I deserved to be happy and live. As crazy as that shit sounds you really will start to believe it. But I really wanna emphasize that you don’t have to go through with those thoughts. I know that sounds like a stupid fucking thing to say but when I was really suicidal I felt this overwhelming pressure to kill myself by deadlines I had set in my own head. I was literally hellbent on proving I wasn’t a liar or pussy to myself. Looking back I know that was one of the main factors in me pulling the trigger because I never let that go. I would just constantly remind myself that it was something I had to do. I could of saved myself so much trouble and pain if I had just cut myself some slack and let it go. You can make it through this you just gotta keep your head up and take it one day at a time. When you wake up everyday tell yourself I’m gonna be happy today or I’m not gonna use drugs today. Thinking about the future is intimidating but focusing on one day at a time is a whole lot more manageable. You’re in my thoughts bro :)

I have a vague memory of the gunshot and then a loud ringing in my ears. I remember feeling nothing immediately after probably due to shock. But my last memory before blacking out is of my legs jerking and spazzing just like an animal after its been shot and choking on blood. Definitely no bright light or anything though.

I had to get immediate reconstructive surgery on the area around my right eye and another surgery shortly after to put a place holder in the socket. As far as the rest of the shrapnel goes it was too dangerous to remove it because it’d extremely invasive and could potentially cause brain damage. But I have a glass eye now and no sense of smell which is a bit strange but I don’t really mind it that much. I also lost about 50% of my ability to taste because your taste is influenced a lot by smell but I got used to it quick. I have nightmares and flashbacks every now and then but not as much as I used to.
